records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וְנֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נִקְשְׁרָ֖ה בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֶּאֱהָבֵ֥הוּ יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, when he finished speaking to Saul, and [the] soul of Jonathan was bound to [the] soul of David, and loved him Jonathan as his [own] soul.
pieces: When David had finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan's life became bound up with David's life, and Jonathan loved him as he loved himself.

L.1: And it happened, when he had finished speaking to Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

R.1: David finished talking with Saul. Then Saul's son Jonathan felt closely joined to David. He loved David as much as he loved himself.

decisions.choice: the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David: Jonathan was deeply attached to David
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" means a person's life and inner self. The same picture of one life bound to another is used of Jacob and Benjamin in Genesis 44:30. It describes a close and lasting attachment.

decisions.choice: loved him as his own soul: loved him as he loved himself
decisions.reason: "As his own soul" means "as himself" (compare Deuteronomy 13:7). The words are repeated in verse 3 and 20:17. Love in this book is also the word for loyalty given to a leader: all Israel and Judah "loved" David (verse 16), and Saul's servants "love" him (verse 22). Jonathan's love is personal, and it is also the loyalty of a king's son to the man who will be king (23:17).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text includes 17:55-18:5 and the other passages of this chapter
alternatives: the shorter Greek text without these verses
decisions.reason: The main early Greek manuscript (Codex Vaticanus) has a shorter form of chapters 17 and 18. Among other passages it lacks 17:55-18:5, 18:10-11, 18:17-19 and 18:29b-30. Some think that this shorter form is older and that the Hebrew text joins two accounts of how David came to Saul's court; others think the Greek shortened the story to smooth over its repetitions. The Hebrew text is translated here in full. Reviewers should check the evidence before this sentence is marked reviewed.

decisions.choice: Jonathan's life became bound up with David's life (Balanced); felt closely joined to David (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Soul" in modern speech suggests the spiritual part of a person, while the Hebrew word means the whole self and life. Readable adds that Jonathan is Saul's son, which the reader learned in chapters 13 and 14.

records.heading: Jonathan makes a covenant with David

records.source: וַיִּקָּחֵ֥הוּ שָׁא֖וּל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְלֹ֣א נְתָנ֔וֹ לָשׁ֖וּב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And took him Saul on the day the that, and not did he let him return [to the] house of his father.
pieces: From that day on Saul kept David with him and would not let him go back to his father's house.

L.2: And Saul took him on that day and did not let him return to his father's house.

R.2: From that day on, Saul kept David at his court. He did not let him go back home to his father's family.

decisions.choice: Saul took him: David now served at the king's court
decisions.reason: Samuel had warned that a king would take Israel's sons into his service (8:11). David had gone back and forth between Saul and his father's flocks (17:15); from now on he stays with Saul.

decisions.choice: From that day on ... kept David with him
decisions.reason: "Took him" means Saul took David into his service. Balanced and Readable say that he kept him, and Readable names the court.

records.source: וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִ֑ית בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ אֹת֖וֹ כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: And made Jonathan and David a covenant, because he loved him as his [own] soul.
pieces: Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as he loved himself.

L.3: And Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.

R.3: Jonathan made a covenant with David, a solemn promise to be loyal to each other, because he loved him as much as he loved himself.

decisions.choice: made a covenant: a binding agreement of loyalty, sworn before God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says a covenant was "cut". A covenant bound two parties with an oath, often in Yahweh's name (20:8, 42). This covenant is recalled in 20:8-17 and 23:18, and David keeps it after Jonathan's death for the sake of Jonathan's son (2 Samuel 9:1-7; 21:7).

decisions.choice: because he loved him: Jonathan loved David
decisions.reason: The pronouns are unclear on their own, but verse 1 and the next verse show that Jonathan is the one who loves and who takes the lead.

decisions.choice: a covenant, a solemn promise to be loyal to each other
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "covenant" and explains it once for new readers.

records.source: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁ֣ט יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן אֶֽת־הַמְּעִיל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְדָוִ֑ד וּמַדָּ֕יו וְעַד־חַרְבּ֥וֹ וְעַד־קַשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְעַד־חֲגֹרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And stripped himself Jonathan [of] the robe that [was] on him and gave it to David, and his garments, and even his sword and even his bow and even his belt.
pieces: Jonathan stripped off the robe he had on and handed it to David, together with his battle clothing, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.

L.4: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that [was] on him and gave it to David, and his garments, even his sword and his bow and his belt.

R.4: Jonathan took off the robe he had on and gave it to David. He also gave him his soldier's clothes, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.

decisions.choice: the robe and the weapons: the gift of a king's son
decisions.reason: The robe was a fine outer garment worn by people of rank (2:19; 15:27; 24:5). Jonathan, the heir to Saul's throne, gives David his own robe and his weapons. The gift seals the covenant, and it points ahead to Jonathan's words in 23:17: "you will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you."

decisions.choice: his garments: his tunic or battle dress
decisions.reason: The word means a garment, here worn with weapons; it is used of Saul's battle clothing in 17:38-39, which David could not wear. Its exact form is not known.

decisions.choice: his sword and his bow: Jonathan's own weapons
decisions.reason: In 13:22 only Saul and Jonathan had swords in Israel. David had refused Saul's armor (17:38-39); Jonathan's gift is freely given and freely taken. Jonathan was known for his bow (20:20, 36; 2 Samuel 1:22).

decisions.choice: battle clothing (Balanced); soldier's clothes (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word goes with weapons here, so Balanced and Readable say what kind of clothing it was.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלָחֶ֤נּוּ שָׁאוּל֙ יַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַיְשִׂמֵ֣הוּ שָׁא֔וּל עַ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י כָל־הָעָ֔ם וְגַ֕ם בְּעֵינֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃פ
records.gloss: And went out David; in all that sent him Saul he succeeded, and set him Saul over the men of the war; and it was good in [the] eyes of all the people and also in [the] eyes of [the] servants of Saul.
pieces: David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he succeeded every time, so Saul put him in charge of the fighting men. This pleased all the people, and Saul's officials too.

L.5: And David went out; wherever Saul sent him, he succeeded, and Saul set him over the men of war. And it was good in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of Saul's servants.

R.5: Saul sent David out on many missions, and every time David did well. So Saul made him a leader over the soldiers. All the people were glad about this, and so were Saul's officials.

decisions.choice: he succeeded: he acted wisely and so did well
decisions.reason: The verb means both acting with good sense and having success as a result. It is a key word of this chapter (verses 14, 15 and 30), and it shows David's skill as well as Yahweh's help (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the men of war: the soldiers
decisions.reason: The phrase means fighting men, the army Saul kept with him (13:2; 14:52).

decisions.choice: Saul's servants: the men of the king's court
decisions.reason: The "servants" of a king are his officials and officers, free men who serve at court (16:15-17; 22:6-9).

decisions.choice: Saul's officials
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "officials" for the king's servants, so that readers do not think of household slaves. Literal keeps "servants".

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗ם בְּשׁ֤וּב דָּוִד֙ מֵהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה הַנָּשִׁ֜ים מִכָּל־עָרֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָשִׁ֣יר וְהַמְּחֹל֔וֹת לִקְרַ֖את שָׁא֣וּל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בְּתֻפִּ֥ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּבְשָׁלִשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And it was, when they came, when returned David from striking down the Philistine, and came out the women from all [the] cities of Israel to sing and the dances to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.
pieces: As the army was coming home, when David returned from killing the Philistine, the women came out from every town in Israel to meet King Saul, singing and dancing with tambourines, with joyful songs and with musical instruments.

L.6: And it happened, as they were coming, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, that the women came out from all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.

R.6: When the soldiers were coming home after David had killed the Philistine, women came out of all the towns of Israel to meet King Saul. They sang and danced with joy, and they played tambourines and other musical instruments.

decisions.choice: the women came out singing and dancing: a victory welcome
decisions.reason: Women met returning warriors with songs, dances and tambourines (Exodus 15:20-21; Judges 11:34). The welcome is for the king and his army after the victory over the Philistines in chapter 17.

decisions.choice: when they came: the army coming home after the battle of chapter 17
decisions.reason: "They" are Saul's men returning from the pursuit of the Philistines (17:52-53). "The Philistine" is Goliath (17:50-51).

decisions.choice: three-stringed instruments: an instrument whose exact kind is not known
decisions.reason: The word comes from the number three. It may name a three-stringed lute, a triangle, cymbals, or a dance in three beats. It is found only here.

decisions.choice: musical instruments
decisions.reason: Since the exact instrument is not known, Balanced and Readable use a general term; Literal follows the word's link with "three".

decisions.choice: the army (Balanced); the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they". Balanced and Readable name who was coming.

records.heading: Saul becomes jealous of David

records.source: וַֽתַּעֲנֶ֛ינָה הַנָּשִׁ֥ים הַֽמְשַׂחֲק֖וֹת וַתֹּאמַ֑רְןָ הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בַּאֲלָפָ֔יו וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And sang the women who [were] playing, and they said, Struck down Saul his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
pieces: As they celebrated, the women sang to one another, \q "Saul has struck down his thousands, \q and David his tens of thousands."

L.7: And the women who were celebrating sang to one another and said, \q "Saul has struck down his thousands, \q and David his ten thousands."

R.7: As they celebrated, the women sang this song back and forth: \q "Saul has killed his thousands, \q and David his tens of thousands."

decisions.choice: sang: sang in turn, one group answering another
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "answer". Used of singing, it means a song sung in parts, one group of singers replying to another (Exodus 15:21; Ezra 3:11).

decisions.choice: who were celebrating: playing, dancing and making merry
decisions.reason: The verb means to play or laugh. Here it is the joyful dancing and music of a festival, as when David celebrates before Yahweh in 2 Samuel 6:5, 21.

decisions.choice: his thousands ... his ten thousands: a poetic pair that may praise both men
decisions.reason: "Thousand" and "ten thousand" are a common pair in Hebrew poetry, where the second line raises the first (Deuteronomy 32:30; Psalm 91:7; Micah 6:7). The women may mean that both men have won great victories. Saul hears the song as setting David above him (verse 8), and the Philistines remember it in the same way (21:12; 29:5).

decisions.choice: "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands" at Balanced; Readable "killed"
decisions.reason: The song is quoted again in 21:12 and 29:5, so its wording is kept short and fixed at each level for those verses. Literal keeps "ten thousands" as the Hebrew plural; Balanced uses the English "tens of thousands". Each level sets the song in two lines after the line that introduces it.

records.source: וַיִּ֨חַר לְשָׁא֜וּל מְאֹ֗ד וַיֵּ֤רַע בְּעֵינָיו֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָתְנ֤וּ לְדָוִד֙ רְבָב֔וֹת וְלִ֥י נָתְנ֖וּ הָאֲלָפִ֑ים וְע֥וֹד ל֖וֹ אַ֥ךְ הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it burned to Saul greatly, and was evil in his eyes the thing the this, and he said, They have given to David ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands, and still for him [is] only the kingdom.
pieces: Saul was furious, and this saying displeased him. "They have credited David with tens of thousands," he said, "and me with mere thousands. What more is left for him but the kingdom?"

L.8: And Saul was very angry, and this word was evil in his eyes, and he said, "They have given to David ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands, and what more [is there] for him but the kingdom?"

R.8: Saul became very angry. He did not like this song at all. He said, "They say that David has killed tens of thousands, but I have killed only thousands. The only thing left for him to take is my kingdom!"

decisions.choice: it burned to Saul: Saul became angry
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of anger as burning or heat (11:6; 20:30).

decisions.choice: and still for him only the kingdom: what more can he get except the kingdom?
decisions.reason: The words are short and sharp: "and still for him only the kingdom." Saul means that the people have given David everything except the throne, and that the throne will be next. He does not know of David's anointing (16:13), but Samuel had told him that Yahweh would give the kingdom to someone better than he (15:28).

decisions.choice: they have given: they have credited, ascribed
decisions.reason: "Given" here means "assigned in the song": the women have given David the larger number.

decisions.choice: a question: "What more is left for him but the kingdom?"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a statement, but English says this most naturally as a question. Readable keeps it a statement.

decisions.choice: mere thousands
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "mere" to bring out the contrast Saul draws between the two numbers.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֖וּל עוֹיֵ֣ן אֶת־דָּוִ֑ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָהָֽלְאָה׃ס
records.gloss: And was Saul eyeing David from the day the that and onward.
pieces: From that day on, Saul watched David with suspicion.

L.9: And Saul was eyeing David from that day and onward.

R.9: From that day on, Saul watched David closely because he did not trust him.

decisions.choice: eyeing: watching with suspicion and jealousy
decisions.reason: The verb, found only here, is made from the word for "eye". It means to keep an eye on someone with distrust. The written Hebrew letters and the way the text is read aloud differ slightly here, but both give this sense.

decisions.choice: because he did not trust him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the suspicion in the rare verb.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַתִּצְלַ֣ח רוּחַ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀רָעָ֤ה׀אֶל־שָׁאוּל֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֣א בְתוֹךְ־הַבַּ֔יִת וְדָוִ֛ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ כְּי֣וֹם׀בְּי֑וֹם וְהַחֲנִ֖ית בְּיַד־שָׁאֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And it was on [the] next day, and rushed [a] spirit of God evil upon Saul, and he prophesied in [the] midst of the house, and David [was] playing with his hand as day by day, and the spear [was] in [the] hand of Saul.
pieces: The next day a harmful spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved inside the house while David was playing the lyre, as he did every day. Saul had his spear in his hand.

L.10: And it happened on the next day that an evil spirit of God rushed upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house, while David [was] playing with his hand, as day by day; and the spear [was] in Saul's hand.

R.10: The next day God let an evil spirit take hold of Saul. Saul began to act wildly inside his house, like a man in a trance. David was playing music on the lyre, as he did every day. Saul was holding a spear.

decisions.choice: an evil spirit of God: a harmful spirit that came from God
decisions.reason: Since Yahweh's Spirit left Saul, a spirit "from Yahweh" troubled him (16:14-16, 23; 19:9). The word "evil" can mean morally bad, or harmful and troubling. The text says that God sent it as part of his judgment on Saul (15:23, 28), as he sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem (Judges 9:23). It does not say what kind of being it was.

decisions.choice: rushed upon Saul: the same verb as when God's Spirit came on Saul for good
decisions.reason: The verb "rushed" was used when the Spirit of God came on Saul so that he prophesied and led Israel (10:6, 10; 11:6), and when the Spirit of Yahweh came on David (16:13). Now a harmful spirit rushes on Saul in the same way.

decisions.choice: he prophesied: he behaved in an uncontrolled, frenzied way
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for prophesying, but here it describes the outward behavior of someone gripped by a spirit, speaking and acting out of control (compare 10:10-11; 19:23-24). It does not mean that Saul brought a message from God.

decisions.choice: playing with his hand: playing the lyre
decisions.reason: David had been brought to court to play the lyre when the spirit troubled Saul, and the music brought Saul relief (16:16, 23). Saul's spear was a sign of his rank and was always near him (22:6; 26:7).

decisions.choice: raved (Balanced); act wildly ... like a man in a trance (Readable); the lyre
decisions.reason: "Prophesied" would suggest to most readers that Saul spoke a message from God, which is not the point here, so Balanced and Readable describe the behavior. They name the lyre from 16:16, 23. Literal keeps "prophesied".

decisions.choice: God let an evil spirit take hold of Saul
decisions.reason: Readable makes God the subject to show that the spirit came from him, as 16:14 says.

records.source: וַיָּ֤טֶל שָׁאוּל֙ אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֔ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַכֶּ֥ה בְדָוִ֖ד וּבַקִּ֑יר וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד מִפָּנָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And hurled Saul the spear and said, I will strike David and the wall; and went around David from before him two times.
pieces: Saul hurled the spear, thinking, "I will pin David to the wall." But David escaped from him twice.

L.11: And Saul hurled the spear, and he said [to himself], "I will strike David to the wall." And David turned aside from before him twice.

R.11: Saul threw the spear at David. He thought, "I will pin David to the wall!" But David got out of the way. This happened two times.

decisions.choice: he said: he thought to himself
decisions.reason: "Said" here means said in his mind, as often in Hebrew (verses 17 and 21; Genesis 26:9). "Strike David and the wall" means to drive the spear through David into the wall (19:10).

decisions.choice: hurled: threw the spear
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or cast. Saul throws his spear again at David in 19:10 and at Jonathan in 20:33.

decisions.choice: David turned aside from before him twice: he dodged the spear two times
decisions.reason: "Turned aside" means that David moved out of the spear's way. "Twice" may count this attack and the one in 19:10, which this verse tells in advance, or two throws on this one day.

decisions.choice: thinking (Balanced); He thought (Readable)
decisions.reason: Saul is speaking to himself, not to David, so Balanced and Readable say "thought". Literal adds "[to himself]".

records.source: וַיִּרָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל מִלִּפְנֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד כִּֽי־הָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּמֵעִ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל סָֽר׃
records.gloss: And was afraid Saul from before David, because was Yahweh with him, and from with Saul he had turned aside.
pieces: Saul feared David, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with David and had turned away from Saul.

L.12: And Saul was afraid of David, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him, but from Saul {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had turned away.

R.12: Saul was afraid of David. He could see that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with David, but that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left Saul.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was with David but had turned away from Saul
decisions.reason: "Yahweh is with him" was said of David when he first came to court (16:18) and is repeated in verses 14 and 28. The same verb "turn away" was used in 16:14, when the Spirit of Yahweh left Saul. Saul now sees what Samuel said would happen (15:28).

decisions.choice: afraid: Saul fears David
decisions.reason: The king fears the young man he has put in charge of his soldiers. The fear grows through the chapter: "dreaded" in verse 15, "even more afraid" in verse 29.

decisions.choice: with David ... from Saul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the names where the Hebrew uses pronouns, so that it is clear who is meant.

decisions.choice: He could see that
decisions.reason: Readable adds that Saul recognized this, as verse 28 says.

records.source: וַיְסִרֵ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ ל֖וֹ שַׂר־אָ֑לֶף וַיֵּצֵ֥א וַיָּבֹ֖א לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And removed him Saul from with him and appointed him for himself [as] commander of [a] thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.
pieces: So Saul sent him away from his presence and made him commander of a thousand men. David led the army in its campaigns.

L.13: And Saul removed him from his presence and made him commander of a thousand for himself, and he went out and came in before the people.

R.13: So Saul sent David away from his court and made him commander of a thousand soldiers. David led the soldiers when they went out to fight and when they came home.

decisions.choice: removed him from his presence: Saul sent David away from court
decisions.reason: Saul wants David out of his sight, but by sending him out to fight he gives him even more chances to succeed and to win the people's love (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: commander of a thousand: the leader of one of the army's larger units
decisions.reason: A "thousand" was a unit of the army, whose actual size may have been smaller (8:12; 17:18; see the note at Numbers 1:21). David had already been set over the fighting men (verse 5); now he has a command of his own in the field.

decisions.choice: went out and came in before the people: led the army in its campaigns
decisions.reason: To "go out and come in before" people means to lead them in war (verse 16; Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11). "The people" here is the army, as often in Samuel.

decisions.choice: led the army in its campaigns (Balanced); led the soldiers when they went out to fight and when they came home (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom and say that "the people" are the army.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛ד לְכָל־דָּרְכָ֖ומַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And was David in all his ways succeeding, and Yahweh [was] with him.
pieces: David succeeded in everything he did, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him.

L.14: And David was succeeding in all his ways, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with him.

R.14: David did well in everything he did, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him.

decisions.choice: succeeding in all his ways: acting wisely and doing well in everything
decisions.reason: "Ways" means his undertakings. The verb is the one used in verse 5: David acts with good sense and succeeds.

decisions.choice: and Yahweh was with him: the reason for David's success
alternatives: and also Yahweh was with him
decisions.reason: The two clauses are joined by "and", but the second explains the first, as in verse 12 and 16:18.

decisions.choice: for / because
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the link that the Hebrew "and" implies.

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁר־ה֖וּא מַשְׂכִּ֣יל מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֖גָר מִפָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And saw Saul that he [was] succeeding greatly, and he dreaded from before him.
pieces: When Saul saw how very successful David was, he was in dread of him.

L.15: And Saul saw that he was succeeding greatly, and he dreaded him.

R.15: Saul saw that David was doing very well, and that made Saul even more afraid of him.

decisions.choice: dreaded: was in fear and awe of him
decisions.reason: This verb is a stronger word for fear than the one in verse 12. It can mean to stand in awe or to shrink back in fear.

decisions.choice: even more afraid
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this fear goes beyond the fear of verse 12.

records.source: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִיהוּדָ֔ה אֹהֵ֖ב אֶת־דָּוִ֑ד כִּֽי־ה֛וּא יוֹצֵ֥א וָבָ֖א לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And all Israel and Judah [were] loving David, because he [was] going out and coming in before them.
pieces: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.

L.16: And all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was going out and coming in before them.

R.16: But all the people of Israel and Judah loved David, because he was the one who led them into battle.

decisions.choice: all Israel and Judah: the whole people, with Judah named apart
decisions.reason: Judah, David's own tribe, is named beside Israel, as in 11:8 and 17:52. Later Judah and Israel each make David king separately (2 Samuel 2:4; 5:1-3).

decisions.choice: loved: were devoted and loyal to him
decisions.reason: Love for a leader is loyalty and support (see the note at verse 1). Saul, who is the king, "dreads" David; the people "love" him.

decisions.choice: going out and coming in before them: leading them in war
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" sets the people's love against Saul's dread in verse 15, so Balanced and Readable say "but".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד הִנֵּה֩ בִתִּ֨י הַגְּדוֹלָ֤ה מֵרַב֙ אֹתָהּ֙ אֶתֶּן־לְךָ֣ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ךְ הֱיֵה־לִּ֣י לְבֶן־חַ֔יִל וְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁא֣וּל אָמַ֗ר אַל־תְּהִ֤י יָדִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וּתְהִי־ב֖וֹ יַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And said Saul to David, Here [is] my daughter, the elder, Merab; her I will give to you as wife; only be for me a son of valor and fight [the] battles of Yahweh. And Saul said, Let not be my hand on him, but let be on him [the] hand of [the] Philistines.
pieces: Saul said to David, "My older daughter Merab is here. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be a brave warrior for me and fight the battles of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." For Saul thought, "I will not raise my hand against him. Let the Philistines do that."

L.17: And Saul said to David, "Here [is] my elder daughter Merab; I will give her to you as a wife. Only be a son of valor for me and fight the battles of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." For Saul said [to himself], "Let not my hand be on him, but let the hand of the Philistines be on him."

R.17: One day Saul said to David, "Here is Merab, my older daughter. I will let you marry her. But you must serve me as a brave soldier and fight the wars of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." Saul was thinking, "I will not kill David myself. I will let the Philistines kill him."

decisions.choice: I will give her to you as a wife: the promised reward for killing Goliath
decisions.reason: The men of Israel had said that the king would give his daughter to the man who killed the Philistine (17:25). Saul now offers it, but adds a condition. Merab is named among Saul's daughters in 14:49.

decisions.choice: a son of valor: a brave and able warrior
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a quality means a person who has that quality. The phrase means a brave fighting man (14:52; 2 Samuel 2:7).

decisions.choice: the battles of Yahweh: Israel's wars, fought for Yahweh and with his help
decisions.reason: Israel's wars against its enemies are called Yahweh's wars (25:28; Numbers 21:14), since Yahweh fights for his people (17:47). Saul uses holy words for a plan to get David killed.

decisions.choice: let not my hand be on him: I will not kill him myself
decisions.reason: "Hand on" someone means to attack or harm him (24:7; Genesis 37:27). Saul plans for the Philistines to do what he has failed to do with his spear (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Saul thought (Balanced); Saul was thinking (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, "said" means Saul said it to himself.

decisions.choice: I will not kill David myself. I will let the Philistines kill him.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the hand.

records.heading: Saul's daughters and David

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־שָׁא֗וּל מִ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ וּמִ֣י חַיַּ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת אָבִ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־אֶהְיֶ֥ה חָתָ֖ן לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And said David to Saul, Who [am] I, and who [are] my kin, [the] clan of my father in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?
pieces: David answered Saul, "Who am I, and what is my family, my father's clan in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?"

L.18: And David said to Saul, "Who [am] I, and who [are] my kin, my father's clan in Israel, that I should become son-in-law to the king?"

R.18: David said to Saul, "I am not important, and my family and my father's clan are not important in Israel. I should not become the son-in-law of the king!"

decisions.choice: my kin: my relatives, my family
decisions.reason: The word is usually "life", but the vowels here give the sense "kindred", and it stands beside "my father's clan". Some take it as "my life", that is, "what is my standing?"

decisions.choice: Who am I ...?: a humble answer to a great honor
decisions.reason: People answered an honor with words of humility (9:21; 2 Samuel 7:18). David's family was not of high rank (16:11; 17:28). The question is polite, and it also hints at the problem of verse 23: he has nothing fit to give for a king's daughter.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: Readable turns the rhetorical questions into the statements they imply.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵ֥ת תֵּ֛ת אֶת־מֵרַ֥ב בַּת־שָׁא֖וּל לְדָוִ֑ד וְהִ֧יא נִתְּנָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל הַמְּחֹלָתִ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And it was, at [the] time of giving Merab daughter of Saul to David, and she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as wife.
pieces: But when the time came for Merab, Saul's daughter, to be given to David, she was given instead to Adriel of Meholah as his wife.

L.19: And it happened, at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, that she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.

R.19: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul gave her to a man named Adriel from the town of Meholah instead.

decisions.choice: at the time of giving Merab ... she was given to Adriel: Saul broke his word
decisions.reason: The verse does not say why. Saul's promise was a trap (verse 17), and he could withdraw it when he pleased. Merab and Adriel's sons are mentioned in 2 Samuel 21:8, where the Hebrew text names Michal as their mother.

decisions.choice: the Meholathite: from Abel-meholah
decisions.reason: Adriel came from a town called Meholah, probably Abel-meholah in the Jordan Valley (Judges 7:22; 1 Kings 19:16).

decisions.choice: Adriel of Meholah (Balanced); a man named Adriel from the town of Meholah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where Adriel came from instead of using the clan-like name "Meholathite".

records.source: וַתֶּאֱהַ֛ב מִיכַ֥ל בַּת־שָׁא֖וּל אֶת־דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְשָׁא֔וּל וַיִּשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And loved Michal daughter of Saul David, and they told to Saul, and was right the thing in his eyes.
pieces: Now Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David. When Saul was told about it, he was pleased.

L.20: And Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David; and they told Saul, and the thing was right in his eyes.

R.20: Saul's other daughter Michal loved David. When Saul heard about it, he was glad.

decisions.choice: Michal loved David: a woman's love for a man, seldom told in Hebrew narrative
decisions.reason: The stories of Israel often say that a man loved a woman (Genesis 29:18; 1 Samuel 1:5), but rarely the reverse. Here, and again in verse 28, it is said of Michal. Michal is Saul's younger daughter (14:49). Her love will save David's life (19:11-17).

decisions.choice: the thing was right in his eyes: Saul was pleased
decisions.reason: "Right in his eyes" means that it suited him. Verse 21 tells why: he saw a new way to have David killed.

decisions.choice: they told Saul: it was reported to Saul
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; "they told" means that people reported it.

decisions.choice: Saul's other daughter
decisions.reason: Readable adds "other" so that Michal is not confused with Merab in verse 19.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶתְּנֶ֤נָּה לּוֹ֙ וּתְהִי־ל֣וֹ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ וּתְהִי־ב֖וֹ יַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד בִּשְׁתַּ֛יִם תִּתְחַתֵּ֥ן בִּ֖י הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And said Saul, I will give her to him, and she will be to him a snare, and will be on him [the] hand of [the] Philistines. And said Saul to David, By two you will become my son-in-law today.
pieces: Saul thought, "I will give her to him so that she can be a trap for him, and the Philistines can kill him." So Saul said to David, "Today you have a second chance to become my son-in-law."

L.21: And Saul said [to himself], "I will give her to him, so that she may be a snare to him, and the hand of the Philistines may be on him." And Saul said to David, "By a second [one] you will become my son-in-law today."

R.21: Saul thought, "I will let David marry her. She will be like a trap for him, and the Philistines will kill him." So Saul said to David, "Today you have a second chance to become my son-in-law."

decisions.choice: a snare: a trap
decisions.reason: A snare caught birds and animals; the word is used of anything that leads a person to ruin (Exodus 10:7; Judges 2:3). Saul means the marriage, and the price he will set for it (verse 25), will bring David to his death.

decisions.choice: by two: a second time, that is, a second chance after Merab
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and unclear. It most likely means "a second time" (compare Job 33:14). Others take it as "through the second" (Saul's second daughter) or "in two ways". The main early Greek manuscript does not have these words (see the note at verse 1).

decisions.choice: Saul said: first to himself, then to David
decisions.reason: The first "said" is Saul's thought, as in verse 17; the second is spoken to David.

decisions.choice: Saul thought ... the Philistines can kill him
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the first "said" is thought, and the idiom of the hand is put plainly.

records.source: וַיְצַ֨ו שָׁא֜וּל אֶת־עֲבָדָ֗ודַּבְּר֨וּ אֶל־דָּוִ֤ד בַּלָּט֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֨ה חָפֵ֤ץ בְּךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־עֲבָדָ֖יו אֲהֵב֑וּךָ וְעַתָּ֖ה הִתְחַתֵּ֥ן בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And commanded Saul his servants: Speak to David in secret, saying, Look, delights in you the king, and all his servants love you; and now be son-in-law to the king.
pieces: Then Saul gave orders to his officials: "Speak to David privately and tell him, 'The king is pleased with you, and all his officials love you. Now is the time to become the king's son-in-law.'"

L.22: And Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David in secret, saying, 'Look, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; and now become son-in-law to the king.'"

R.22: Then Saul gave orders to his officials. He said, "Talk to David when no one else is around. Tell him, 'The king likes you, and all his officials love you. You should marry the king's daughter now.'"

decisions.choice: in secret: privately, as if on their own
decisions.reason: The officials are to speak as though giving friendly advice, without saying that the king sent them.

decisions.choice: delights in you ... love you: the king and his court favor you
decisions.reason: "Delight in" means to be pleased with and to want (verse 25 uses the same word for what the king "wants"). "Love" is loyalty and good will, as in verse 16.

decisions.choice: be son-in-law to the king: marry into the king's family
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for a son-in-law or bridegroom and means to become related by marriage. It is repeated through verses 21-27.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the king's servants are court officials.

decisions.choice: marry the king's daughter
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what becoming the king's son-in-law means.

records.source: וַֽיְדַבְּר֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד הַֽנְקַלָּ֤ה בְעֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הִתְחַתֵּ֣ן בַּמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִֽישׁ־רָ֥שׁ וְנִקְלֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And spoke [the] servants of Saul in [the] ears of David the words the these. And said David, [Is it] light in your eyes to be son-in-law to the king, and I [am] a man poor and lightly esteemed?
pieces: Saul's officials spoke these words to David. But David said, "Do you think it is a small thing to become the king's son-in-law? I am only a poor man of no importance."

L.23: And Saul's servants spoke these words in the ears of David. And David said, "Is it a light thing in your eyes to become son-in-law to the king, when I [am] a poor man and lightly esteemed?"

R.23: Saul's officials told David what Saul had said. But David answered, "Becoming the king's son-in-law is a big thing. I am a poor man, and people do not think I am important."

decisions.choice: a light thing ... lightly esteemed: a play on one word
decisions.reason: Both words come from the same root, meaning "light" or "of little weight". David asks if they think marrying into the king's family is a light matter, when he himself is a man of light standing.

decisions.choice: a poor man: he cannot pay a bride-price fit for a king's daughter
decisions.reason: A man who married gave a bride-price to the bride's family (Genesis 34:12; Exodus 22:15-16). David's answer is humble, and it also says that he cannot afford a king's daughter. Saul answers this point in verse 25.

decisions.choice: spoke in the ears of David: told David
decisions.reason: To speak "in someone's ears" means to speak to that person directly.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable turns David's question into the statement it implies.

records.source: וַיַּגִּ֜דוּ עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁא֛וּל ל֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה דִּבֶּ֥ר דָּוִֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And told [the] servants of Saul to him, saying, According to the words the these spoke David.
pieces: Saul's officials told him, "This is what David said."

L.24: And Saul's servants told him, saying, "David spoke according to these words."

R.24: Saul's officials went back to Saul and told him what David had said.

decisions.choice: according to these words David spoke: they report David's answer
decisions.reason: The officials repeat what David said in verse 23, his humility and his poverty.

decisions.choice: told him what David had said
decisions.reason: Readable gives the report as indirect speech.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל כֹּֽה־תֹאמְר֣וּ לְדָוִ֗ד אֵֽין־חֵ֤פֶץ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּמֹ֔הַר כִּ֗י בְּמֵאָה֙ עָרְל֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהִנָּקֵ֖ם בְּאֹיְבֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְשָׁא֣וּל חָשַׁ֔ב לְהַפִּ֥יל אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד בְּיַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Saul, Thus you will say to David: There is no delight for the king in bride-price, except in a hundred foreskins of Philistines, to take vengeance on [the] enemies of the king. And Saul planned to make fall David by [the] hand of [the] Philistines.
pieces: Saul replied, "Say this to David: 'The king wants no bride-price except a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on the king's enemies.'" Saul was planning to have David killed by the Philistines.

L.25: And Saul said, "Thus you shall say to David: 'The king has no delight in a bride-price except a hundred foreskins of Philistines, to take vengeance on the king's enemies.'" And Saul planned to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

R.25: Saul said, "Tell David this: 'The king does not want any money or gifts for his daughter. He wants only the foreskins of one hundred Philistines. That will pay back the king's enemies.'" Saul was really planning to have the Philistines kill David.

decisions.choice: a bride-price: the payment a man gave to his bride's family
decisions.reason: A bride-price was given to the bride's father when a marriage was agreed (Genesis 34:12; Exodus 22:15-16). It could also be paid in service or a great deed (Genesis 29:18; Joshua 15:16). Saul answers David's poverty (verse 23) by asking for a deed instead of wealth.

decisions.choice: a hundred foreskins of Philistines: proof of a hundred Philistines killed
decisions.reason: The foreskin is the fold of skin removed in circumcision. Israel was circumcised and the Philistines were not; "uncircumcised" was a common name for them (14:6; 17:26, 36). Bringing back their foreskins proved how many enemies had been killed, and that they were Philistines.

decisions.choice: to take vengeance on the king's enemies: Saul presents the price as a public duty
decisions.reason: Saul calls the Philistines "the king's enemies", but the narrator tells the real aim at once: to have David killed in the attempt (compare verse 17).

decisions.choice: to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines: to have him killed by them
decisions.reason: "Fall" means fall dead in battle; "by the hand of" means by their power or action.

decisions.choice: any money or gifts for his daughter
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a bride-price is instead of using the term.

decisions.choice: foreskins
decisions.reason: The word is kept at every level. It is plain, not crude, and the point of the story depends on it.

records.source: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ עֲבָדָ֤יו לְדָוִד֙ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיִּשַׁ֤ר הַדָּבָר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א מָלְא֖וּ הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And told his servants to David the words the these, and was right the thing in [the] eyes of David to be son-in-law to the king; and not were fulfilled the days.
pieces: When his officials told David these words, David was pleased with the idea of becoming the king's son-in-law. Before the time was up,

L.26: And his servants told David these words, and the thing was right in David's eyes, to become son-in-law to the king. And the days were not [yet] fulfilled,

R.26: Saul's officials told David what Saul wanted, and David was glad to become the king's son-in-law. Before the time Saul had set was over,

decisions.choice: the days were not yet fulfilled: the time set for the deed had not run out
alternatives: and the days had not yet been completed when ...
decisions.reason: The narrator had not mentioned a deadline, but this shows that one was set. The clause begins the action of verse 27: David acted quickly. The main early Greek manuscript does not have it (see the note at verse 1).

decisions.choice: the thing was right in David's eyes: David was pleased
decisions.reason: The same words were used of Saul in verse 20. Each man is pleased for his own reason.

decisions.choice: his officials (Balanced); Saul's officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 22. Readable names Saul to avoid confusion over whose officials they were.

decisions.choice: the time Saul had set
decisions.reason: Readable says that the days were a time limit Saul had given.

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ׀ה֣וּא וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו וַיַּ֣ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים֮ מָאתַ֣יִם אִישׁ֒ וַיָּבֵ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶת־עָרְלֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְמַלְא֣וּם לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֥וֹ שָׁא֛וּל אֶת־מִיכַ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And arose David and went, he and his men, and struck down among the Philistines two hundred men, and brought David their foreskins, and they gave them in full to the king, to become son-in-law to the king; and gave to him Saul Michal his daughter as wife.
pieces: David got up and went out with his men and killed two hundred Philistine men. He brought their foreskins, and they were counted out in full to the king, so that David could become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal as his wife.

L.27: David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down two hundred men among the Philistines. And David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full to the king, so as to become son-in-law to the king. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.

R.27: David went out with his men and killed two hundred Philistines. David brought their foreskins to the king and counted them out to show that the full number was there. He did this so that he could become the king's son-in-law. So Saul let David marry his daughter Michal.

decisions.choice: two hundred men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "two hundred". The early Greek translation has "a hundred", the number Saul asked for, and David later speaks of the hundred foreskins he paid for Michal (2 Samuel 3:14). In the Hebrew, David gives twice the price asked.

decisions.choice: they gave them in full: the foreskins were counted out before the king
decisions.reason: The verb means to fill or complete: the full number was handed over. The plural "they" may be David and his men, or it may simply mean that the count was made.

decisions.choice: Saul gave him Michal: Saul's trap fails
decisions.reason: Saul had hoped David would die (verse 25). Instead David comes back alive, and Saul has to keep his word. Verse 28 tells why: Yahweh was with David.

decisions.choice: so that David could become (Balanced); He did this so that (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the purpose clear and name David.

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא שָׁאוּל֙ וַיֵּ֔דַע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִם־דָּוִ֑ד וּמִיכַ֥ל בַּת־שָׁא֖וּל אֲהֵבַֽתְהוּ׃
records.gloss: And saw Saul and knew that Yahweh [was] with David, and Michal daughter of Saul loved him.
pieces: Saul saw and understood that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with David, and that his own daughter Michal loved him.

L.28: And Saul saw and knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with David, and that Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.

R.28: Saul now understood that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with David. He also knew that his daughter Michal loved David.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was with David
decisions.reason: What the narrator said in verses 12 and 14 Saul now sees for himself.

decisions.choice: Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him
decisions.reason: The early Greek translation reads "and all Israel loved him" (compare verse 16). The Hebrew text, followed here, repeats Michal's love from verse 20: even Saul's own daughter is on David's side.

decisions.choice: his own daughter Michal (Balanced); his daughter Michal (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "his daughter" for "daughter of Saul", since Saul is the subject. Balanced adds "own" to keep the weight of naming Saul in the Hebrew.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אסֶף שָׁא֗וּל לֵרֹ֛א מִפְּנֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד ע֑וֹד וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֛וּל אֹיֵ֥ב אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And added Saul to be afraid from before David still, and was Saul enemy of David all the days.
pieces: Saul became even more afraid of David, and Saul was David's enemy for the rest of his life.

L.29: And Saul was still more afraid of David, and Saul was an enemy of David all the days.

R.29: Saul became even more afraid of David. For the rest of his life, Saul was David's enemy.

decisions.choice: added to be afraid still: became even more afraid
decisions.reason: "Added" with another verb means to do something more or again. Saul's fear grows from verse 12 to verse 15 and now here.

decisions.choice: all the days: from then on, for the rest of his life
decisions.reason: "All the days" means always, here for as long as Saul lived (compare 31:4-6). The main early Greek manuscript does not have this sentence or verse 30 (see the note at verse 1).

decisions.choice: for the rest of his life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "all the days" means here.

records.source: וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י׀מִדֵּ֣י צֵאתָ֗ם שָׂכַ֤ל דָּוִד֙ מִכֹּל֙ עַבְדֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּיקַ֥ר שְׁמ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃ס
records.gloss: And went out [the] commanders of [the] Philistines, and it was, as often as they went out, succeeded David more than all [the] servants of Saul, and was esteemed his name greatly.
pieces: The commanders of the Philistines kept coming out to fight, and every time they came out, David was more successful than all Saul's other officers. So his name became highly honored.

L.30: And the commanders of the Philistines went out; and it happened, as often as they went out, David succeeded more than all Saul's servants, and his name was highly esteemed.

R.30: The Philistine commanders kept leading their armies out to fight Israel. Every time they did, David had more success than any of Saul's other officers. Everyone thought very highly of David.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the Philistines: the Philistine war leaders
decisions.reason: The word can name rulers or army officers; here they lead the Philistines out to battle (29:3-4). They will remember David's success (21:12; 29:5).

decisions.choice: succeeded: acted wisely and did well
decisions.reason: The key verb of the chapter (verses 5, 14 and 15).

decisions.choice: his name was highly esteemed: he gained a great reputation
decisions.reason: A "name" is a person's reputation. "Esteemed" means precious or highly valued (compare 26:21).

decisions.choice: Saul's other officers
decisions.reason: In battle the king's servants are his officers. Balanced and Readable say "officers" and add "other", since David is one of them; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: Everyone thought very highly of David
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the name.
